[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''Hugh Glasgow''' was born on '''25 July 1786''' in '''County Down, Ireland'''. An obituary published in ''The Reformed Presbyterian and Covenanter'' states that he was born there, came to America in '''1796''' and, while still a young man, joined the Pine Creek, Union, and associated Reformed Presbyterian congregation in western Pennsylvania. He remained connected with that congregation until his death.<ref name="HughObituary">“Hugh Glasgow,” obituary, ''The Reformed Presbyterian and Covenanter'', vol. 13 (April 1875), p. 131; https://archive.org/details/reformedpresbyt10willgoog/page/n161/mode/1up.</ref>

The obituary is direct evidence for Hugh’s reported birthplace, although it was published about nine months after his death rather than during his childhood. No baptismal or other contemporary Irish birth record has yet been identified.

A later family history gives different indirect evidence. William Melanchthon Glasgow wrote that Hugh’s brother John was born “on the farm in County Londonderry, not far from the town of Portglenone.”<ref name="GlasgowHistory">William Melanchthon Glasgow, ''History of the Glasgow Family''; https://www.wikitree.com/photo/pdf/Glasgow-590.</ref>

Portglenone is in County Antrim, close to the boundary with County Londonderry. The description probably places the family farm west of Portglenone, on the County Londonderry side of the boundary.

John’s birthplace has sometimes been used as indirect evidence that Hugh was also born on that farm. The family history does not explicitly say this, however, while Hugh’s obituary expressly names County Down. Hugh’s structured birthplace should therefore remain County Down, marked uncertain if required, until an original Irish record resolves the conflict.

Hugh was approximately nine or ten years old when he emigrated in 1796.

=== Residence in Pennsylvania ===

Census records place a Hugh Glasgow in northern Allegheny County over several decades:

* in '''1830''', at Deer Township, Allegheny County, Pennsylvania;<ref name="Census1830">“United States Census, 1830,” database with images, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XHP6-DP2), Hugh Glasgow, Deer, Allegheny County, Pennsylvania; citing NARA microfilm publication M19, roll 144.</ref>
* in '''1840''', at West Deer Township, Allegheny County;<ref name="Census1840">“United States Census, 1840,” database with images, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XHBQ-PDX), Hugh Glascow, West Deer Township, Allegheny County, Pennsylvania; citing NARA microfilm publication M704, roll 439.</ref>
* in '''1850''', at West Deer Township;<ref name="Census1850">“United States Census, 1850,” database with images, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M44D-V7R), Hugh Glasgow, West Deer, Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, family 177; citing NARA microfilm publication M432.</ref> and
* in '''1860'''.<ref name="Census1860">“United States Census, 1860,” database with images, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MXP8-DK5), entry for Hugh Glasgow.</ref>

The 1830 and 1840 censuses name only the head of household. Their household age categories should be compared with later records before assigning unnamed household members as particular children.

The residence sequence is consistent with Hugh’s obituary, which states that he remained associated with the Pine Creek and Union congregation throughout his adult life.

=== Wife ===

A cemetery transcription records '''Margaret Miller''' as the wife of Hugh Glasgow. It states that she died on '''23 November 1851''', in the fifty-ninth year of her age.<ref name="Cemetery">“Depreciation Lands Museum Cemetery, Hampton Township, Pennsylvania,” cemetery transcription, entries for Hugh Glasgow and Margaret Miller Glasgow; https://freepages.rootsweb.com/~njm1/genealogy/03dlmcem.htm.</ref>

This supports identifying Margaret Miller as Hugh’s wife, although a photograph of the original monument or another contemporary marriage or probate record would provide stronger evidence.

The transcription records Hugh nearby and states that he died on 10 July 1874 in the eighty-eighth year of his age.<ref name="Cemetery" />

=== Twin Sister ===

The family history identifies Hugh’s twin sister as '''Nancy''' and states that both twins lived to be eighty-eight and died in the same year.<ref name="GlasgowHistory" />

Hugh’s obituary instead identifies his twin sister as '''Margaret Cunningham'''. It states that her farm adjoined Hugh’s and that she died on '''14 January 1874''', both twins then being in their eighty-eighth year.<ref name="HughObituary" />

The obituary is unusually specific, supplying Margaret’s married surname, death date and neighbouring residence. It is therefore strong evidence that the twin was known as Margaret Cunningham.

Nancy was historically used as a form of Ann or Anne. It was not ordinarily a form of Margaret, whose common forms included Maggie, Meg, Peg and Peggy.<ref name="Nicknames">Hallie Borstel Kirchner, “An Introduction to Nicknames,” ''Vita Brevis'', American Ancestors, 12 April 2021; https://vitabrevis.americanancestors.org/2021/04/introduction-to-nicknames.</ref>

Possible explanations for the conflicting names include:

* the family history recorded the wrong given name;
* the obituary recorded the wrong given name;
* Nancy or Margaret was a middle or commonly used name; or
* two different women were confused by one of the accounts.

Margaret Cunningham should not be merged with another woman or assigned a husband solely from her married surname. A gravestone, probate record, church record, deed or death notice naming her husband and relationship to Hugh is still required.

=== Death and Burial ===

Hugh was confined to his bed for approximately eighteen months before his death on '''10 July 1874'''.<ref name="HughObituary" />

The cemetery transcription independently records the same death date and states that he was in the eighty-eighth year of his age.<ref name="Cemetery" />

Hugh was buried at the cemetery now identified as '''Depreciation Lands Museum Cemetery''' in Hampton Township, Allegheny County, Pennsylvania.<ref name="Cemetery" /> His Find a Grave memorial also associates him with this burial place.<ref>{{FindAGrave|23399484}}</ref>

Hugh was eighty-seven years old when he died, fifteen days before his eighty-eighth birthday.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-540]] is assessed at 91% (proved). Hugh’s 1827 will expressly names a son Hugh. The established family account places Hugh-539 in this particular family, with a feasible 1786 generation and no evidenced rival son of that identity. The combined named-son and family identification supports confidence.

Complete father-profile proposition91%; the will gives no age or residence. County Down and twin claims are not established by it.

Next useful test: Use Hugh’s obituary or estate correspondence to verify the son’s identity.

Source basis already held: [https://www.ancestry.com/imageviewer/collections/8802/images/005537856_00276?pid=1733435 Allegheny County Will Book 3, no.252, pp.492–493: Hugh Glasgo, signed 29 March 1827, probate 25 April 1831; recorded image re-read; household check, not a parentage clause]; [https://www.wikitree.com/photo.php/0/0a/Glasgow-590.pdf William Melanchthon Glasgow, History of the Glasgow Family, scanned pp.2–3: named Hugh–McCullough parents and youngest son; descendant household and migration; re-read 17 October 2026]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.



=== Birthplace Conflict ===

The two principal narrative sources do not provide equal evidence concerning Hugh’s birthplace:

* Hugh’s obituary expressly states that he was born in County Down.<ref name="HughObituary" />
* The family history states that his brother John was born on the family farm in County Londonderry near Portglenone, but does not explicitly say that Hugh was born there.<ref name="GlasgowHistory" />
* Both sources place the family’s emigration in 1796.

County Down should not be replaced with County Londonderry solely from the birthplace reported for John.

Possible explanations include:

* the family lived in County Down in 1786 and later moved to the Portglenone-area farm;
* Hugh’s mother was temporarily staying with relatives or other acquaintances in County Down when the twins were born;
* the obituary’s contributor misunderstood the family’s Irish geography; or
* the later family history incorrectly assumed that all siblings were born on the same farm.

A baptismal entry, contemporary family Bible or other Irish record naming Hugh and his twin would be needed to resolve the issue.

=== Hospital-Birth Theory ===

No evidence has been found that Hugh and his twin were born in a hospital.

Belfast’s Poor House Infirmary opened in 1774, but it was a general charitable infirmary rather than a specialist maternity hospital. Belfast’s first dedicated lying-in hospital did not open until 1794, eight years after Hugh’s birth.<ref name="BelfastHealthcare">“The NHS at 70: Belfast before Universal Healthcare,” ''Clifton House'', 6 July 2018; https://cliftonbelfast.com/news/the-nhs-at-70-belfast-before-universal-healthcare/.</ref>

County infirmaries also operated in late eighteenth-century Ulster, including institutions at Londonderry, Lisburn and Downpatrick. These principally treated illness and injury rather than routine childbirth.<ref name="UlsterInfirmaries">Andrew Sneddon, “State Intervention and Provincial Health Care: The County Infirmary System in Late Eighteenth-Century Ulster,” ''Irish Historical Studies'' 38, no. 149 (May 2012): 5–21; https://doi.org/10.1017/S0021121400000596.</ref>

A history of midwifery in Ulster states that even in 1806 nearly all women gave birth at home, apart from the relatively small number admitted to lying-in hospitals in Belfast or Dublin.<ref name="MidwiferyHistory">John F. O’Sullivan, “Two Hundred Years of Midwifery 1806–2006,” ''Ulster Medical Journal'' 75, no. 3 (September 2006): 213–222; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1891762/.</ref>

A difficult twin birth may have required extra local assistance, but the available evidence gives no reason to connect Hugh’s reported County Down birthplace with a hospital.

=== Age Terminology ===

The obituary’s statement that Hugh and his twin were in their eighty-eighth year is consistent with Hugh’s stated dates.<ref name="HughObituary" />

A person entered the eighty-eighth year of life upon completing eighty-seven years. Hugh was therefore eighty-seven, not eighty-eight, when he died.

The family history’s statement that the twins lived to be eighty-eight was probably a less exact restatement of this older form of age description rather than a substantial disagreement.

=== Source Assessment ===

The April 1875 obituary is the strongest available source for:

* Hugh’s exact birth date;
* County Down as his reported birthplace;
* immigration in 1796;
* his lifelong congregational association;
* his final illness;
* his death date; and
* Margaret Cunningham as his twin sister.

The cemetery transcription independently corroborates Hugh’s death date and age description and identifies Margaret Miller as his wife.

The family history remains useful but was compiled later and conflicts with the obituary concerning Hugh’s birthplace and his twin’s given name. Its claims should be checked against contemporary records wherever possible.

=== Research Priorities ===

Further research should seek:

* a baptismal record for Hugh and his twin dated near 25 July 1786;
* Presbyterian or Reformed Presbyterian registers in County Down;
* records near Portglenone and across the County Londonderry boundary;
* passenger, port or naturalisation records concerning the family’s 1796 migration;
* a photograph or full transcription of Hugh and Margaret Miller Glasgow’s monument;
* a marriage record for Hugh Glasgow and Margaret Miller;
* probate records for Hugh and Margaret;
* complete household analysis of the 1830 and 1840 censuses;
* the full 1850 and 1860 households;
* records naming Margaret Cunningham’s husband;
* Margaret Cunningham’s burial or probate record; and
* Pine Creek and Union congregational session or membership records.

=== Research Conclusion ===

The April 1875 obituary directly states that Hugh Glasgow was born in County Down on '''25 July 1786''', emigrated to America in '''1796''' and remained associated with the Pine Creek and Union Reformed Presbyterian congregation until his death.

It also directly identifies '''Margaret Cunningham''' as his twin sister.

A cemetery transcription corroborates Hugh’s death on '''10 July 1874''', records that he was in his eighty-eighth year and identifies '''Margaret Miller''' as his wife.

The family history’s County Londonderry evidence relates directly to Hugh’s brother John rather than to Hugh. County Down remains the best currently sourced birthplace, although the conflict should remain documented until a contemporary Irish record is found.
